passage: Tuesday evening. Karthik came to the library corner today, the second-year I promised to mentor. I was ready to give the speech I once got: do competitive coding, do the hard problems, join every club. Then I stopped and asked, "What do you want out of this year?" Karthik said, "An internship, any internship, next summer." That changed everything. Competitive coding is not what I did for my own internship. I got it by building two small projects and putting them on a page. So I drew a simple sketch for Karthik: two projects, one clean resume, a few applications by January. It felt odd advising something different from my own story, but it made sense. Jasleen

qa.q: What does Karthik want out of this year?
qa.a: Karthik wants an internship, any internship, for next summer.

qa.q: How did Jasleen feel about advising something different from Jasleen's own story?
qa.a: Jasleen felt a little uncertain, since it felt odd to advise something other than what had worked before, but it made sense for Karthik's goal.

qa.q: What could Jasleen do to check that the plan works, and why?
qa.a: Jasleen could ask Karthik to review the plan in a month, because a real target like applications by January can be measured.

qa.q: How might Karthik feel when Jasleen asks what Karthik wants?
qa.a: Karthik probably feels listened to and clearer about the year ahead, since the advice now fits the goal.

grounding: A mentoring student asks a second-year what they want and tailors advice to that goal instead of repeating their own path.

Reena: didi, you said you'd mentor me. where do I start? should I do DSA like you did?
Rajni: before that. what do you actually want by next summer?
Reena: honestly? a first internship. anything real. my parents keep asking
Rajni: what kind? coding, research, design?
Reena: I liked the UI project in 1st year more than the coding contests tbh
Rajni: ok that changes things. I did 400 DSA problems because I wanted product companies. that might not be your road
Reena: so what is?
Rajni: for a UI internship: 2 good design projects, a simple portfolio, and some front-end basics. DSA only enough for the test rounds
Reena: that sounds way less scary 😅
Rajni: we'll plan it properly on sunday. bring 3 companies you'd love to intern at
Reena: ok!! thank you didi 🙏

qa.q: How many DSA problems did Rajni do?
What was Rajni thinking when she said 'that might not be your road'?
qa.a: She seemed concerned not to push her own path, seeing that it suited her goals and not necessarily Reena's.

qa.q: What else could Rajni do on Sunday?
qa.a: Look at Reena's three companies together and work backward from what their interns need.

qa.q: How does the conversation feel to Reena?
qa.a: Reena feels relieved that the plan fits her interest in design and sounds far less scary than 400 problems.

grounding: Shows a final-year mentor asking a junior's real goal, a first design internship, and tailoring advice to it instead of repeating her own path.

subtype: Approach: starting with the junior's actual goal [Thinking]
passage:
At the tea stall outside the polytechnic in Sagar, Dhruv, in his final year, waited for his junior Tushar with a notebook full of placement tips: aptitude tests, group discussions, the interview questions he'd faced.
Tushar arrived and pulled up a stool, and Dhruv caught himself. He had been about to hand over his own path. 'First tell me,' he said. 'What do you want, two years from now?'
Tushar hesitated. 'Honestly? Not a company job. I want to go back to our village and run my father's dairy better. Cold storage, maybe. Proper records.'
Dhruv closed the placement notebook. None of it fitted. 'Okay. Then your first internship should be at a dairy cooperative, not an IT firm. And we should look for the refrigeration elective.'
Tushar's face opened into a grin. 'Nobody ever asked me that before.'
They spent the next hour listing cooperatives within fifty kilometres.

qa.q: What does Tushar want to do in two years?
qa.a: Go back to the village and run his father's dairy better.

qa.q: Why did Dhruv close the placement notebook, and how might he have felt?
qa.a: He felt a little surprised and humbled, seeing that his own tips didn't fit Tushar's goal.

qa.q: What could Dhruv help Tushar with next?
qa.a: Write to two or three nearby dairy cooperatives about internships and plan which electives fit the goal.

qa.q: What is it like for Tushar to be asked about his own goal?
qa.a: Tushar feels seen and happy, grinning because nobody had asked before.

grounding: Shows a senior asking a junior what he actually wants, a better family dairy, and tailoring advice to it instead of passing on placement tips.
